text.p: Italian debt instruments hit selling and sank suddenly in late trade after failing to make progress on the upside and due to volatility in U.S. markets.
The February 2007 Btp ended 63 basis points in the red at 102.33 with yield at 6.51 percent and the spread over the benchmark Bund at 98 basis points.
The September futures contract on LIFFE was 89 basis points weaker at 137.13 having tumbled alongside the Bund as it broke out of a recent 137.80-138.10 trading range.
After failure to make upside progress the market eventually broke to the downside.

The break triggered "stop after stop after stop with no bids," one broker said. "It feels toppish now having tried that resistance at 138.10 and failed. So the correction everyone was waiting for looks like it's arrived."
One dealer said the cash market also a looked a bit heavy after today's Treasury auction of a total 4.0 trillion lire of three and five year Btps.
The market was now set to wait for U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
